# Plain Ballot

> Free, open-source, nonpartisan voter guide. A voter picks the issues they care about and sets a dial for each; Plain Ballot matches every race on their ballot (California, Nov 3, 2026) to those priorities and shows an exact, verified quote behind every claim.

Matching is deterministic arithmetic in the browser, not AI. Candidate positions are researched by independent AI agents on models from different companies; a position is published only when the agents agree and its quote is found word for word on the cited page. Party labels are hidden until the voter asks.

## Key pages

- [Home](https://plainballot.com): pick issues, set dials, enter an address
- [How it works](https://plainballot.com/methodology): the method, the agreement rules, and what isn't covered

## Source and data

- [Source code (AGPL-3.0)](https://github.com/n8peace/plainballot)
- [Dial wording](https://github.com/n8peace/plainballot/blob/main/lib/issues.ts): the 18 issues and how each end is worded
- [Matching](https://github.com/n8peace/plainballot/blob/main/lib/match.ts): the scoring arithmetic
- [Researched positions](https://github.com/n8peace/plainballot/tree/main/data/positions): one JSON file per contest, each claim with a quote and source URL
- [Research file schema](https://github.com/n8peace/plainballot/blob/main/data/positions.schema.json)
- [Architecture](https://github.com/n8peace/plainballot/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)
- [Contributing](https://github.com/n8peace/plainballot/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
